title: Epochal batch embed scheduler with client idempotency
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Current embed ingestion exposes two distinct failure modes at scale: (1) large streaming uploads that rely on single-request atomicity frequently incur partial commits on transient infra failures, and (2) clients retrying batches create duplicate vectors without reliable cross-request deduplication. We need a hybrid streaming->batch ingestion path that provides low latency for small/streaming producers, high throughput for bulk imports, and strong client-visible idempotency guarantees.
goal: Ship a scheduler and job lifecycle that accepts both streaming and batch uploads, groups work into epochal batches with causal checkpoints, and exposes client-supplied idempotency references so producers can safely retry without duplication. End-state: stable async jobs with per-epoch commit markers, resume semantics, 1.5x throughput improvement for bulk loads, and <0.5% duplicate vector rate under realistic retry patterns.
design_summary: We propose an 'epochal' model: each ingest job is assigned an increasing epoch token for the target shard-range. Producers can supply a client_id and optional client_epoch to gate commits. The scheduler groups incoming records into epoch windows (configurable by size/time), writes to a write-ahead 'epoch log' with per-record opaque tokens, and enqueues an async commit job when thresholds hit. The commit job uses a two-phase commit: (1) atomic append to epoch log + ephemeral checkpoint in durable KV, (2) bulk write to vector store with monotonic commit marker. On retry, the idempotency lookup uses (client_id, client_epoch) to resolve whether the epoch completed; if partially committed, reconciler will determine missing offsets and reapply only gaps. Backpressure is signaled to streaming producers via stream windowing and per-client credit tokens. Metrics and tracing hooks added for epoch latency, commit size, duplicates avoided, and client retry outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/embeds/bulk accepts streaming payloads with optional 'client_id' and 'client_epoch' and returns a job_id immediately
Scheduler groups records into epoch windows and persists epoch log entries to durable store before acknowledging job creation
Async commit job writes with at-least-once safety but job reconciler reduces duplicates to <0.5% under synthetic 3x retry storm
Clients can resume aborted shipments by providing job_id and offset; server resumes from last committed offset and returns deterministic progress
Load test shows >=1.5x throughput for large batched imports compared to current streaming path at 90th percentile latency within SLO
End-to-end observability: per-job tracing, epoch-level latency and size dashboards, and alerting on excessive duplicate ratio
comments: 2026-02-18 - Spike complete: prototype scheduler that groups by size and time exists in branch feat/epochal-scheduler. Baseline microbenchmark shows grouping efficiency improvements for small 10KB records.

2026-02-25 - Design review with PM (Sophie Klein) and Infra (Daniel Park). Decision: use durable KV (consensus store) for epoch checkpoints rather than relying on object store because of ordering guarantees.
2026-03-02 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-embed-svc/pull/1832 implementing epoch log write path and job enqueue. Waiting on infra owner review (cc @infra-oncall).

2026-03-05 - Prototype metrics: epoch creation latency median 12ms, commit job median 220ms for 5k-record batches. Duplicate rate observed 1.2% under single-failure retry; target <0.5%. Added reconciler tasks to reapply only missing offsets.
2026-03-08 - Blocker: KV quota on staging causing ephemeral checkpoint writes to fail intermittently. Ops is provisioning additional capacity. Workaround: throttle epoch creation to 5/s.

2026-03-10 - Mateocode review comments addressed. Added explicit per-client credit tokens and backpressure signals in streaming protocol. Next: full load test and integration test for resume semantics.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Durable epoch log becomes a hotspot under many small producers. Mitigation: shard epoch log by client hash and add write-ahead batching in-memory within host before flush.

Risk: Reconciler growth — if many partial epochs accumulate, reconciliation cost grows. Mitigation: cap partial epochs per-client and auto-fail long-running partials with compensating restarts and clear audit logs.
Risk: Consumer-side duplicates due to at-least-once write to vector store. Mitigation: embed a per-record opaque-id and use vector-store-side upsert semantics with idempotency window during commit.
Risk: Client epoch semantics confusion. Mitigation: doc changes and API client SDKs will include helper methods to manage client_epoch lifecycle.
Risk: Performance regression for small streaming producers. Mitigation: default to micro-batch epoch thresholds tuned by workload and expose knobs per-customer in Dedicated/Private plans.
